purpose: One entry point (src/web/buggy.mjs) that lets a world drive a vehicle over LiDAR or generated ground: the dynamics cartridge adapted to the feel layer's fixed-step contract, the terrain cartridge and the access checks, dependency-free and deterministic, 0 CPU when parked.

Four-contact rigid-body vehicle dynamics (spring-damper suspension, slip-curve tyres, drive, brake, Ackermann steering) for driving LiDAR and generated ground; a JS reference module for the world and a CuPy/NumPy batch mirror for pair runs (semi-implicit Euler against RK4).

Ground under each wheel: terrain heights and normals across tile edges, surface class from open data layers with friction and rolling resistance, illustrative soft-ground sinkage, water crossings flagged, and collision with solids. The world passes its own heightAt, so heights are sampled one way only.

Driver feel: keyboard, gamepad and touch input shaped on the fixed step, chase and driver cameras, speed, gradient and heading readout, mount and dismount, recorded drives with sha256, guided site tours; 0 frames when parked.

Checks a driven trace or a designed road for delivery vehicles: gradient, cross-slope, bend radius, swept path, gates, deck grounding, structures and soft ground; answers whether an abnormal load reaches its destination; gives a fixed-step drive-through for a sales view.
